Question: What do you think, is Iron Dome effective or useless? How does the Iron Dome actually work?
Old_Answer: Iron Dome missile defense system…….How does it work? The Iron Dome was specially designed to protect against a range of incoming short-range threats. Basically, it has three components, which is the case for most air defense systems: radar that detects the incoming rocket; a command-and-control system that processes that information and then activates the third component, which is the interceptor — basically a missile whose role is to destroy the other rocket. Is Iron dome effective? The all-weather system was specially designed to help combat shorter-range weapons like the rockets fired from Gaza. The Iron Dome uses radar to identify and then intercepts & destroys the incoming threats before they can cause damage. More than 2,000 rockets have been fired towards Israel by Hamas and other Palestinian militant groups in five days. But about 90% of the rockets have been intercepted by Israel’s flagship Iron Dome missile defense system. Can it be relied upon completely? Iron Dome can detect and intercept anything, but it was designed for unsophisticated weapons like rockets. It cannot intercept ballistic missiles coming from Iran. So that’s the reason why it is effective technically — but strategically, it doesn’t change the fact that the Israelis cannot rely on it completely. Not saying that the Iron Dome is useless, I just think it’s like an insurance option. It’s a great way to reassure the citizens, also to avoid total disruption of daily life. But at the end of the day, this cannot be the only option. Iron Dome is considered among the most advanced defense systems in the world.

Question: What are some unknown heroes of India worthy of a salute?
Old_Answer: ‘Mastar Moshai’ Sujit Chattopadhyay is nearly 80 years old and lives in a village named Ausgram in West Bengal’s Bardhaman district. Back in November 2021, he was presented with the prestigious Padma Shri award in the field of Literature and Education. He taught for 39 years and at the age of 60yers retired as a school principal. One day, 3 girls walked 20 kilometres to meet him. They were tribal girls who wanted to learn from him. He demanded fees from them, but only Re 1 each! So in 2004, he started teaching again post his retirement. He turned his veranda into a school – ‘Sadai Fakirer Pathshala’ and dedicated his post-retirement life to educating underprivileged tribal children. As word spread to nearby localities that there is a teacher who teaches kids for a yearly fee of Re 1, innumerable eager kids arrived at his door. Pathshala soon enrolled as many as 350 students! Mastar Moshai’s day would start at 6 AM and end at 6 PM. 80% of the attendance was by tribal girls. He taught social sciences to secondary levels and a degree course in Bengali to undergraduate students. His school has a solid attendance system made complete with regular PTA meetings. Over the years, his students have become professors, heads of departments and IT professionals. They call him to inform their achievements, which fills his heart with pride. Now his fee has increased to Rs 2/year, but that’s just a mark of respect from students. Sujit Chattopadhyay’s contribution to the education and empowerment of underprivileged children remains unmatched even to this day. Salute to his noble work!

Old_Answer: The “Shrew’s Fiddle,” was used to punish women in medieval times. One was a large hole for the neck and the other two were smaller holes which fastened the wrists in front of the face A bell was sometimes attached to this portable pillory, to alert townspeople that the victim was approaching so that she might be mocked and otherwise humiliated. Another version was a "double fiddle" by which two people could be attached together face-to-face, forcing them to talk to each other. They were not released until the argument had been resolved. The Medieval Ages was not really kind to women.
